transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I’m here because when I start eating certain comfort foods, I just can’t seem to stop. I’ll tell myself, “Maria, that’s enough now,” but then my hand goes right back to the pot anyway. It feels like I’m not really in control once I get started.

Can you describe what happens when you start eating these comfort foods? Does it feel like you’re eating much more rapidly than normal, and is there a point where you realize you’ve eaten a lot more than most people would in a similar period?

Yes… I’ve always been a slow eater, usually. But when this happens, it’s different. I’ll be standing there by the counter and eating fast, just bite after bite. I’m hardly even tasting it before the next bite is already in my mouth. Then I look and realize I’ve eaten much more than I meant to.
When you’re eating like this, do you feel like you can’t stop or control how much you’re eating once you start?
Yes. Once I start, it feels like I can’t make myself stop. I’ll tell myself, Maria, that’s enough, but then my hand just goes right back to the pot anyway.
Does this eating behavior cause you distress, or does it interfere with your daily life in any way?

It does upset me, yes. I still do my usual things—I go to Mass, I sing in choir, I keep up with my home. But after one of those afternoons, I feel embarrassed, and I might just stay in and not call anyone. I don’t want people to know.
Do these episodes of eating this way usually happen when you’re feeling stressed, upset, or dealing with strong emotions?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a clear pattern like that. Sometimes I feel a little down afterward, but before it starts… I don’t always know what sets it off.
When you’re eating this way, do you feel a complete loss of control, like you’re unable to stop eating or manage how much you consume, even if you wanted to?

Yes, that’s how it feels. I’ll tell myself, Maria, that’s enough now, but then I still reach for more, like my hand just goes back to the pot before I can stop it. It feels like I’m not really in charge once I get started.
